title: Anchoring: choosing a spot, scope and holding
h1: Anchoring: the spot, the scope, the hold
lead: A secure anchorage comes from three decisions: where you drop, how much chain you let out and whether the anchor has really set. This guide walks through each one.
description: How to anchor a yacht: choosing a sheltered bay with good holding, how much chain to use, setting the anchor, checking it holds and taking shore lines.
summary: Pick a bay sheltered from the forecast wind, with sand or mud and room to swing.
Let out at least 4 to 5 times the depth in chain, more if wind is coming.
Lower the anchor, lay chain while going astern, then set it under reverse power and check with a transit.
Rig a snubber, set an anchor alarm and, if you can, swim over the anchor to look.
